questions.q: Let& $P = \left[\begin{cases}\dfrac{3}{2} & \dfrac{1}{2} \\ - \dfrac{1}{2} & \dfrac{3}{2}\end{cases}\right], A = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]$~and~$Q = PAP^{T}$.~If~$P^{T}Q^{2007}P = \left[\begin{cases}a & b \\ c & d\end{cases}\right]$then~$2a + b - 3c - 4d$& is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given:

$P = \left[\begin{cases}\dfrac{3}{2} & \dfrac{1}{2} \\ - \dfrac{1}{2} & \dfrac{3}{2}\end{cases}\right]$

$∴ PP^{T} = \left[\begin{cases}\dfrac{3}{2} & \dfrac{1}{2} \\ - \dfrac{1}{2} & \dfrac{3}{2}\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{cases}\dfrac{3}{2} & - \dfrac{1}{2} \\ \dfrac{1}{2} & \dfrac{3}{2}\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ PP^{T} = I$

Now,

$P^{T}\left(PAP^{T}\right)2007P = P^{T}\mathop{\left(PAP^{T}\right)\left(PAP^{T}\right)\left(PAP^{T}\right) . . . \left(PAP^{T}\right) ⏟}_{2007times}P$

$⇒ P^{T}\left(PAP^{T}\right)2007P = A^{2007}$

Now,

$A = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]A^{2} = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]A^{3} = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right] ⋮ ⋮ ⋮ ⋮ ⋮ ⋮ ⋮ ⋮ A^{2007} = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 2007 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]$

So,

$⇒ P^{T}\left(PAP^{T}\right)2007P = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 2007 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ P^{T}QP = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 2007 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}a & b \\ c & d\end{cases}\right]$

So,

$a = 1, b = 2007, c = 0, d = 1$

$2a + b + 3c - 4d = 2 + 2007 - 4 = 2005$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
\left|A\right| = \left|\begin{cases}1 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 & 4 \\ 1 & - 1 & 3\end{cases}\right| = \left(\left(9 + 4\right) - 1\left(3 - 4\right) + 2\left(- 1 - 3\right)\right) = 13 + 1 - 8 = 6$
\left|adjB\right| = \left|adjadjA\right| = {\left|A\right|}^{{\left(n - 1\right)}^{2}} = {\left|A\right|}^{4} = {\left(36\right)}^{2}$

\left|adjB\right|\left|C\right| = \dfrac{36 \times 36}{{3}^{3} \times 6} = 8$

questions.q: Let $A = \left[\begin{cases}2 & 1 & 2 \\ 6 & 2 & 11 \\ 3 & 3 & 2\end{cases}\right]$ and $P = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 2 & 0 \\ 5 & 0 & 2 \\ 7 & 1 & 5\end{cases}\right]$. The sum of the prime factors of \left|P^{- 1}AP - 2I\right|$ is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let, $y = \left|P^{- 1}AP - 2I\right|$

$⇒ y = \left|P^{- 1}AP - 2P^{- 1}P\right|$

$⇒ y = \left|\left(P^{- 1}I\right) ( A - 2I ) P\right|$

$⇒ y = \left|P^{- 1}I\right| | A - 2I | | P |$

We know that, \left|A\right| = 1\left|A^{- 1}\right|$.

$⇒ y = | A - 2I |$

$⇒ y = \left|\begin{cases}2 & 1 & 2 \\ 6 & 2 & 11 \\ 3 & 3 & 2\end{cases}\right| - \left|\begin{cases}2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ y = \left|\begin{cases}0 & 1 & 2 \\ 6 & 0 & 11 \\ 3 & 3 & 0\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ y = 0 - \left(0 - 33\right) + 2 \left($18 - 0\right)$

$⇒ y = 69$

Now, prime factor of $69$ is $3$ and $23$.

So, sum $= 26

$

questions.q: If \left[\begin{cases}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{cases}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{cases}1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right] \ldots . \left[\begin{cases}1 & n - 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 78 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right],$ then the inverse of \left[\begin{cases}1 & n \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]$ is:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given& \left[\begin{cases}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{cases}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{cases}1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right] . . . . \left[\begin{cases}1 & n - 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 78 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]$

And, we have~\left[\begin{cases}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{cases}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 1 + 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]$

Also,~\left[\begin{cases}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{cases}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{cases}1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{cases}1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]$

$= \left[\begin{cases}1 & 6 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 1 + 2 + 3 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ \left[\begin{cases}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{cases}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{cases}1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right] . . . . \left[\begin{cases}1 & n - 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 1 + 2 + 3 + . . . . + n - 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ \left[\begin{cases}1 & 1 + 2 + 3 + . . . . + n - 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 78 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]$

Using the sum of first~$n$~natural numbers i.e.~$1 + 2 + 3 + . . . + n = \dfrac{n\left(n + 1\right)}{2},$~we get

$\dfrac{n ( n - 1 )}{2} = 78$

$⇒ n^{2} - n - 156 = 0$

$⇒ \left(n - 13\right)\left(n + 12\right) = 0$

$⇒ n = 13$~or~$n = - 12$ (reject as $n$~is a natural number)
$∴$ We have to find inverse of \left[\begin{cases}1 & 13 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]$

Which can be find by~using~$A^{- 1} = adjA\left|A\right|$

Now,~\left|A\right| = \left|\begin{cases}1 & 13 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right| = 1 - 0 = 1$

${A}_{11} = 1, {A}_{12} = - 13, {A}_{21} = 0, {A}_{22} = 1$

Hence,~$adjA = \left[\begin{cases}1 & - 13 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]$

$∴A^{- 1} = \left[\begin{cases}1 & - 13 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right] .$

$

questions.q: Let $A = \left(\begin{cases}4 & - 2 \\ \alpha & \beta\end{cases}\right)$. If ${A}^{2} + \gammaA + 18I = O$, then $det \left(A\right)$ is equal to _______.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given $A = \left[\begin{cases}4 & - 2 \\ \alpha & \beta\end{cases}\right] ⇒ det\left(A\right) = 4\beta + 2\alpha$

Characteristic equation of the matrix is

$\left[\begin{cases}4 - \lambda & - 2 \\ \alpha & \beta - \lambda\end{cases}\right] = 0$

$⇒ 4\beta + {\lambda}^{2} - \left(\beta + 4\right)\lambda + 2\alpha = 0$

$⇒ {\lambda}^{2} - \left(\beta + 4\right)\lambda + 2\alpha + 4\beta = 0$

Comparing with given equation ${A}^{2} + \gammaA + 18I = 0$, we get

$⇒ \gamma = - \left(\beta + 4\right) \text{ and } 2\alpha + 4\beta = 18$

Hence $det \left(A\right) = 4\beta + 2\alpha = 18$

questions.q: Let $A$~and $B$~be two $3 \times 3$~real matrices such that~  \left(A^{2} - B^{2}\right)$ is invertible matrix. If $A^{5} = B^{5}$ and~$A^{3}B^{2} = A^{2}B^{3},$~then the value of the determinant of the matrix $A^{3} + B^{3}$ is equal to :$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let& $C = A^{2} - B^{2}; \left|C\right| \ne 0$

and~$A^{5} = B^{5} . . . \left(1\right)$

$A^{3}B^{2} = A^{2}B^{3} . . . \left(2\right)$

Subtracting equation~ \left(2\right)$~from~ \left($1\right)$, we get~$A^{5} - A^{3}B^{2} = B^{5} - A^{2}B^{3}$

$⇒ $A^{3}\left($A^{2} - B^{2}\right) + $B^{3}\left($A^{2} - B^{2}\right) = O$

Post multiplying inverse of $A^{2} - B^{2}:$

$A^{3} + B^{3} = O ⇒ \left|$A^{3} + B^{3}\right| = 0$

questions.q: Let $x, y, z > 1$~and~$A = \left[\begin{cases}1 & \log_{\mathrm{x}}y & \log_{\mathrm{x}}z \\ \log_{\mathrm{y}}x & 2 & \log_{\mathrm{y}}z \\ \log_{\mathrm{z}}x & \log_{\mathrm{z}}y & 3\end{cases}\right]$.~Then \left|adj \left(adj A^{2}\right)\right|$ is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given:

$A = \left[\begin{cases}1 & \log_{\mathrm{x}}y & \log_{\mathrm{x}}z \\ \log_{\mathrm{y}}x & 2 & \log_{\mathrm{y}}z \\ \log_{\mathrm{z}}x & \log_{\mathrm{z}}y & 3\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ A = \left[\begin{cases}1 & \dfrac{logy}{logx} & \dfrac{logz}{logx} \\ \dfrac{logx}{logy} & 2 & \dfrac{logz}{logy} \\ \dfrac{logx}{logz} & \dfrac{logy}{logz} & 3\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ A = \dfrac{1}{logxlogylogz}\left[\begin{cases}logx & logy & logz \\ logx & 2logy & logz \\ logx & logy & 3logz\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ \left|A\right| = \dfrac{1}{logx \cdot logy \cdot logz}\left|\begin{cases}logx & logy & logz \\ logx & 2logy & logz \\ logx & logy & 3logz\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ \left|A\right| = \dfrac{logx \cdot logy \cdot logz}{logx \cdot logy \cdot logz}\left|\begin{cases}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 3\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ \left|A\right| = \left|\begin{cases}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 2\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ \left|A\right| = 2$

Now,

\left|adj \left(adj A^{2}\right)\right| = \left|adj A^{2}\right|2 = \left|A^{2}\right|4 = \left|A\right|8 = {2}^{8}$

$

We know that characteristic equation of matrix& $A$~is given by,~

\left|A - \lambdaI\right| = 0$

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}1 - \lambda & 2 \\ - 2 & - 5 - \lambda\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ {λ}^{2} + 4\lambda = 1$

$⇒ A^{2} + 4A = I$

Multiplying by~$2$~both side we get,

$⇒ 2A^{2} + 8A = 2I ⋯ \left(1\right)$

Given that~$\alphaA^{2} + \betaA = 2I ⋯ \left(2\right)$

Now on Comparing equation~ \left(1\right) \text{ and } \left(2\right)$~we get

$\alpha =2, \beta =8$

$∴ \alpha + \beta =10

$

questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & {\left[\mathrm{A}\left(\operatorname{adj}\left(\mathrmA^{-1}\right)+\operatorname{adj}\left(\mathrmB^{-1}\right)\right)^{-1} \cdot \mathrm{~B}\right]^{-1}} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{~B}^{-1} \cdot\left(\operatorname{adj}\left(\mathrm{~A}^{-1}\right)+\operatorname{adj}\left(\mathrmB^{-1}\right)\right) \cdot \mathrmA^{-1} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{~B}^{-1} \operatorname{adj}\left(\mathrm{~A}^{-1}\right) \mathrmA^{-1}+\mathrmB^{-1}\left(\operatorname{adj}\left(\mathrm{~B}^{-1}\right)\right) \cdot \mathrmA^{-1} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{~B}^{-1}\left|\mathrm{~A}^{-1}\right| \mathrm{I}+\left|\mathrmB^{-1}\right| \mathrm{IA}^{-1} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{~B}^{-1}}{|\mathrm{~A}|}+\frac{\mathrmA^{-1}}{|\mathrm{~B}|} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\operatorname{adjB}}{|\mathrm{B}||\mathrm{A}|}+\frac{\operatorname{adj}}{|\mathrm{A}||\mathrm{B}|} \\ & =\frac{1}{|\mathrm{~A}||\mathrm{B}|}(\operatorname{adjB}+\operatorname{adj} \mathrm{A})\end{aligned}$

questions.solution:
Since given matrix $A$ is invertible $⇒ \left|A\right| \ne 0$
~

questions.q: Let $P$~be a square matrix such that $P^{2} = I - P$. For $\alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta \in \mathbb{N}$, if $P^{α} + P^{β} = \gammal - 29P$~and $P^{α} - P^{β} = \deltal - 13P$, then $\alpha + \beta + \gamma - \delta$& is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$P$~be a square matrix such that $P^{2} = I - P$,

Now solving~$P^{2} = I - P$~we get,

$⇒ P^{4} = \left(I - P\right) \left($I - P\right)$

$⇒ P^{4} = I + P^{2} - 2P$

$⇒ P^{4} = I + I - P - 2P = 2I - 3P$

Now solving,~$P^{4} \cdotP^{2} = P^{6} = 2I - 5P + 3P^{2}$~

$⇒ P^{6} = 2I - 5P + 3 \left(I - P\right) = 5I - 8P$...~\left(i\right)$

Similarly~$P^{8} = 13I - 21P$~...~ \left(ii\right)$

Now adding~ \left($ii\right) + \left(i\right)$~we get,

$P^{8} + P^{6} = 18I - 29P$

Now subtracting~ \left(ii\right) - \left(i\right)$~we get,

$P^{8} - P^{6} = 8I - 13P$

Now comparing with~$P^{α} - P^{β} = \deltal - 13P & P^{α} + P^{β} = \gammal - 29P$~we get,

$\alpha =8, \beta =6, \gamma =18, \delta =8$

Hence,~$\alpha + \beta + \gamma - \delta =8 + 6 + 18 - 8 = 24

$

questions.q: If $A$ is a square matrix of order 3 such that $\operatorname{det}(A)=3$ and $\operatorname{det}\left(\operatorname{adj}\left(-4 \operatorname{adj}\left(-3 \operatorname{adj}\left(3 \operatorname{adj}\left((2 \mathrm{~A})^{-1}\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)=2^{\mathrm{m}} 3^{\mathrm{n}}$, then $\mathrm{m}+2 \mathrm{n}$ is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & |\mathrm{A}|=3 \\ & \mid \operatorname{adj}\left(-4 \operatorname{adj}\left(-3 \operatorname{adj}\left(3 \operatorname{adj}\left((2 \mathrm{~A})^{-1}\right)\right)\right) \mid\right. \\ & \mid-4 \operatorname{adj}\left(-\left.3 \operatorname{adj}\left(3 \operatorname{adj}(2 \mathrm{~A})^{-1}\right)\right|^2\right. \\ & 4^6\left|\operatorname{adj}\left(-3 \operatorname{adj}\left(3 \operatorname{adj}(2 \mathrm{~A})^{-1}\right)\right)\right|^2 \\ & 2^{12} \cdot 3^{12}\left|3 \operatorname{adj}(2 \mathrm{~A})^{-1}\right|^8 \\ & 2^{12} \cdot 3^{12} \cdot 3^{24}\left|\operatorname{adj}(2 \mathrm{~A})^{-1}\right|^8\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & 2^{12} \cdot 3^{36}\left|(2 \mathrm{~A})^{-1}\right|^{16} \\ & 2^{12} \cdot 3^{36} \frac{1}{|2 \mathrm{~A}|^{16}} \\ & 2^{12} \cdot 3^{36} \frac{1}{2^{48}|\mathrm{~A}|^{16}} \\ & 2^{12} \cdot 3^{36} \frac{1}{2^{48} \cdot 3^{16}} \\ & \frac{3^{20}}{2^{36}}=2^{-36} \cdot 3^{20} \\ & \mathrm{~m}=-36 \quad \mathrm{n}=20 \\ & \mathrm{~m}+2 \mathrm{n}=4\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let $a, b, c \in R$ be all non-zero and satisfies~$a^{3} + b^{3} + c^{3} = 2$. If the matrix~$A = \left[\begin{cases}a & b & c \\ b & c & a \\ c & a & b\end{cases}\right]$~satisfies $A^{T}A = I,$~then a value of $abc$ can be
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$∵ A^{T}A = I$

$⇒ \left[\begin{cases}a & b & c \\ b & c & a \\ c & a & b\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{cases}a & b & c \\ b & c & a \\ c & a & b\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ \left[\begin{cases}a^{2} + b^{2} + c^{2} & ab + bc + ac & ab + bc + ac \\ ab + bc + ac & a^{2} + b^{2} + c^{2} & ab + bc + ac \\ ab + bc + ac & ab + bc + ac & a^{2} + b^{2} + c^{2}\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]$

On comparing each element both sides, we get

$a^{2} + b^{2} + c^{2} = 1 \text{ and } ab + bc + ca = 0 . . . . . . . . . \left(i\right)$

We know that~$a^{3} + b^{3} + c^{3} - 3abc = \left(a + b + c\right) \left(a^{2} + b^{2} + c^{2} - ab - bc - ac\right)$.

$⇒ 2 - 3abc = \left($a + b + c\right)\left($1 - 0\right)$~(from equation~ \left($i\right)$)

$⇒ 2 - 3abc = \left($a + b + c\right) . . . . . . . . . \left($ii\right)$

Now, we also know that~ \left(a + b + c\right)2 = a^{2} + b^{2} + c^{2} + 2\left(ab + bc + ca\right)$.

$⇒ \left(a + b + c\right)2 = 1 + 2 \left(0\right)$~(from equation~ \left(i\right)$)

$⇒ a + b + c = \pm1$

Putting it in equation~ \left($ii\right)$, we get

$2 - 3abc = $\pm$1$

$⇒ 3abc = 2 ∓ 1$

$⇒ abc = $\dfrac{1}{3}\text{or}$abc = 1

$

questions.q: If $A = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 5 \\ \lambda & 10\end{cases}\right], A^{- 1} = \alphaA + \betaI$~and $\alpha + \beta = - 2$, then $4{α}^{2} + {β}^{2} + {λ}^{2}$& is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$A = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 5 \\ \lambda & 10\end{cases}\right], A^{- 1} = \alphaA + \betaI$~and $\alpha + \beta = - 2$,

Now solving by using characteristic equation, we get
$| A - k | = 0 ⇒ \left|\begin{cases}1 - k & 5 \\ \lambda & 10 - k\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ k^{2} - 11k + 10 - 5\lambda = 0$

$⇒ A^{2} - 11A + ( 10 - 5\lambda ) I = 0$~{by putting $k = A}

$⇒ A^{- 1} = \dfrac{1}{10 - 5\lambda} ( - A + 11I )$

Now on comparing with~$A^{- 1} = \alphaA + \betaI$~we get,

$⇒ \alpha = - \dfrac{1}{10 - 5\lambda}, \beta = \dfrac{11}{10 - 5\lambda}$

And given,

$\alpha + \beta = - 2 ⇒ \lambda = 3, \alpha = \dfrac{1}{5}, \beta = \dfrac{- 11}{5}$

Hence, the value of~$4{α}^{2} + {β}^{2} + {λ}^{2} = 14

questions.q: If $A = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]$ and $M = A + A^{2} + A^{3} + \ldots + A^{20},$~then the sum of all the elements of the matrix $M$ is equal to _______.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have,& $A = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]$ and $M = A + A^{2} + A^{3} + \ldots + A^{20}$

Now,~$A^{2} = A . A = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{cases}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ A^{3} = A^{2} . A = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{cases}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 3 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]$

.

.

.

.

$A^{n} = \left[\begin{cases}1 & n & \dfrac{n\left(n + 1\right)}{2} \\ 0 & 1 & n \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]$

So, required sum

$= 20 \times 3 + 2\mathop{∑ r}_{r = 1}^{20} + \mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{20} \left(\dfrac{r \left($r + 1\right)}{2}\right)

$= 20 \times3 + 2\mathop{∑ r}_{r = 1}^{20} + \dfrac{1}{2}\mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{20}r^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}\mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{20}r$

$= 20 \times3 + \dfrac{5}{2}\mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{20}r + \dfrac{1}{2}\mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{20}r^{2}$

$= 20 \times3 + \dfrac{5}{2} \left(\dfrac{20 \times 21}{2}\right) + \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{20 \times 21 \times 41}{6}\right)

\left[$∵ \mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{n}r = $\dfrac{n \left($n + 1\right)}{2}, \mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{n}$r^{2} = $\dfrac{n \left(n + 1\right) \left(2n + 1\right)}{6}\right]

$= 60 + 5 \left(5 \times21\right) + \left($5 \times7 \times41\right)$

$= 60 + 525 + 1435$

$= 2020$

$

questions.q: Let $A$ be a non-singular matrix of order 3 . If $\operatorname{det}(3 \operatorname{adj}(2 \operatorname{adj}((\operatorname{det} A) A)))=3^{-13} \cdot 2^{-10}$ and $\operatorname{det}(3 \operatorname{adj}(2 \mathrm{~A}))=2^{\mathrm{m}} \cdot 3^{\mathrm{n}}$, then $|3 \mathrm{~m}+2 \mathrm{n}|$ is equal to $\qquad$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & |3 \operatorname{adj}(2 \operatorname{adj}(|A| A))|=\mid 3 \operatorname{adj}\left(2|A|^2 \operatorname{adj}(A) \mid\right. \\ & =\left.\left|3.2^2\right| A\right|^4 \operatorname{adj}\left(\left.\operatorname{adj}(A)\left|=2^6 3^3\right| A\right|^{12}|A|^4\right. \\ & =2^6 3^3|A|^{16}=2^{-10} 3^{-13} \\ & \Rightarrow|A|^{16}=2^{-16} 3^{-16} \Rightarrow|A|=2^{-1} 3^{-1}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \text { Now }|3 \operatorname{adj}(2 \mathrm{~A})|=\left|3.2^2 \operatorname{adj}(\mathrm{A})\right| \\ & =2^6 3^3|\mathrm{~A}|^2=2^{-\mathrm{m}} 3^{-\mathrm{n}} \\ & \Rightarrow 2^6 3^3 2^{-2} 3^{-2}=2^{-\mathrm{m}} 3^{-\mathrm{n}} \\ & \Rightarrow 2^{-\mathrm{m}} 3^{-\mathrm{n}}=2^4 3^1 \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{m}=-4, \mathrm{n}=-1 \\ & \Rightarrow|3 \mathrm{~m}+2 \mathrm{n}|=|-12-2|=14\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The number of matrices of order $3 \times 3$, whose entries are either $0$~or $1$& and the sum of all the entries is a prime number, is _______.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let the matrix be& \left[\begin{cases}a & b & c \\ d & e & f \\ g & h & i\end{cases}\right]$

Since the elements can be either of~$0\text{or}1$, so

$a + b + c + d + e + f + g + h + i = 2 / 3 / 5 / 7$

For sum as~$2$, the number of cases will be~$\dfrac{9 !}{2 ! 7 !} = 36$

For sum as~$3$, the number of cases will be~$\dfrac{9 !}{3 ! 6 !} = 84$

For sum as~$5$, the number of cases will be~$\dfrac{9 !}{5 ! 4 !} = 126$

For sum as~$7$, the number of cases will be~$\dfrac{9 !}{2 ! 7 !} = 36$

Total required matrix will be~$282$

$

questions.q: If $A = \left[\begin{cases}0 & - tan  \left(\dfrac{θ}{2}\right)\\ tan \$left(\dfrac{θ}{2}\right) \text{ and } 0\end{cases}\right]$ and \left({I}_{2} +$A\right)\left({I}_{2} -A\right)- 1 = \left[\begin{cases}a & - b \\ b & a\end{cases}\right],$~then $13\left(a^{2} + b^{2}\right)$ is equal to _____ .$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$A = \left[\begin{cases}0 & - tan\dfrac{θ}{2} \\ tan\dfrac{θ}{2} & 0\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ I + A = \left[\begin{cases}1 & - tan\dfrac{θ}{2} \\ tan\dfrac{θ}{2} & 1\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ I - A = \left[\begin{cases}1 & tan\dfrac{θ}{2} \\ - tan\dfrac{θ}{2} & 1\end{cases}\right]\left\{∴ | I - A | = \sec^{2}\theta / 2\right\}$

$⇒ \left(I - A\right)- 1 = \dfrac{1}{\sec^{2}\dfrac{θ}{2}}\left[\begin{cases}1 & - tan\dfrac{θ}{2} \\ tan\dfrac{θ}{2} & 1\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ \left(I + A\right)\left(I - A\right)- 1 = \dfrac{1}{\sec^{2}\dfrac{θ}{2}}\left[\begin{cases}1 & - tan\dfrac{θ}{2} \\ tan\dfrac{θ}{2} & 1\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{cases}1 & - tan\dfrac{θ}{2} \\ tan\dfrac{θ}{2} & 1\end{cases}\right]$

$= \dfrac{1}{\sec^{2}\dfrac{θ}{2}}\left[\begin{cases}1 - \tan^{2}\dfrac{θ}{2} & - 2tan\dfrac{θ}{2} \\ 2tan\dfrac{θ}{2} & 1 - \tan^{2}\dfrac{θ}{2}\end{cases}\right]$

$a = \dfrac{1 - \tan^{2}\dfrac{θ}{2}}{\sec^{2}\dfrac{θ}{2}}$

$b = \dfrac{2tan\dfrac{θ}{2}}{\sec^{2}\dfrac{θ}{2}}$

$∴ a^{2} + b^{2} = 1$

$∴ 13\left(a^{2} + b^{2}\right) = 13$

questions.q: Let $A$ be a $2 \times 2$ real matrix and $I$ be the identity matrix of order $2 .$ If the roots of the equation $| A - xI | = 0$ be $- 1$ and $3,$ then the sum of the diagonal elements of the matrix $A^{2}$ is _____.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$Given: $| A - xI | = 0$ have roots $- 1$ and $3$.

Let, $A = \left[\begin{cases}a & b \\ c & d\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ A - xI = \left[\begin{cases}a & b \\ c & d\end{cases}\right] - \left[\begin{cases}x & 0 \\ 0 & x\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ A - xI = \left[\begin{cases}a - x & b \\ c & d - x\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ \left|A - xI\right| = \left(a - x\right)\left(d - x\right) - bc$

$⇒ \left|A - xI\right| = ad - ax - dx + x^{2} - bc$

$⇒ \left|A - xI\right| = x^{2} - \left($a + d\right)x + \left($ad - bc\right)$

Sum of roots, $a + d = 2$

Product of roots, $ad - bc = - 3$

Now finding matrix $A^{2}$,

$⇒ A^{2} = $\$left[\begin{cases}a & b \\ c & d\end{cases}\right] $\times \left[\begin{cases}$a & b \\ c & d\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ A^{2} = $\$left[\begin{cases}a^{2} + bc & ab + bd \\ ac + cd & bc + d^{2}\end{cases}\right]$

Sum of diagonal elements, $S = a^{2} + bc + bc + d^{2}$

$⇒ S = a^{2} + 2bc + d^{2}$

$⇒ S = ( a + d{)}^{2} - 2 \left(ad - bc\right)$

$⇒ S = ( 2{)}^{2} - 2 \left(-3\right)$

$⇒ S = 4 + 6$

$⇒ S = 10$

$
